newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan fund looks to reduce debt - business group.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan fund looks to reduce debt - business group.

text.p: Morocco's social security fund has launched a restructuring plan aimed at reducing its debt and improving its management, a Casablanca-based businessmen's association said on Wednesday.
In a report of a meeting between the association and fund officials, the businessmen's group said the fund mobilised billions of dirhams and needed to be managed with "absolute rigour".
Officials from the association and the state-run Caisse Nationale de Securite Sociale (CNSS) met late last month.

According to the figures published by the business group, Confederation Generale des Entreprises du Maroc (CGEM), the fund in 1996 collected 3.25 billion dirhams ($346.5 million) from those paying into it to receive family allowances.
The year before, it collected 2.99 billion dirhams, the report said.
It said the CNSS distributed to its subscribers 2.02 billion dirhams in 1996 against 1.52 billion dirhams in 1995. It added that the fund had a debt of 5.0 billion dirhams ($532 million) in 1996.

An estimated 1.1 million employees, out of Morocco's workforce of more than eight million, are affiliated to the fund, according to the CGEM, which added that CNSS subscribers' average salary was 2,758 dirhams per month.

"An estimated 80 percent of firms affiliated to the fund are micro-enterprises and 50 percent of employees do not realise enough hours to reach the minimum wage required to subscribe to the fund," it added.
The average minimum wage in Morocco is 1,700 dirhams.

According to the CGEM report, fund officials told the joint meeting that an "upgrading policy" would continue in 1997 and the family allowance system would be extended to remote rural areas "despite hostile psychological obstacles".
